target_profile.system_boundary: github.com/hashicorp/raft as captured (single module; module path github.com/hashicorp/raft). One Raft instance is one node of a cluster; the module also ships NetworkTransport/TCPStreamLayer/InmemTransport, an in-memory FSM/store for tests, and the raft-compat and fuzzy nested modules. FSM, LogStore, StableStore and SnapshotStore are caller-supplied interfaces, so durability of applied state is outside this module.
protocol_contexts: leader election with optional pre-vote (PreVoteDisabled, transport WithPreVote)
log replication via AppendEntries and InstallSnapshot
single-uncommitted-configuration membership change with Voter/Nonvoter/Staging suffrage
leadership transfer via TimeoutNow and candidateFromLeadershipTransfer
protocol versions 0..3 with legacy AddPeerDeprecated/RemovePeerDeprecated entries
external_interfaces: Transport with optional WithPreVote, WithClose, WithPeers, SetHeartbeatHandler
ownership: the raft main goroutine started by run() owns raftState, configurations, leaderState and all RPC handling through the rpcCh consumer channel
one followerReplication goroutine per peer plus one heartbeat goroutine owns replication progress and the commitment match table
the NetworkTransport spawns one connection-handler goroutine per inbound connection and may invoke the registered heartbeat callback on that goroutine
the fsm goroutine consumes fsmMutateCh and the snapshot goroutine consumes fsmSnapshotCh
selection_injection: Config.LocalID/ProtocolVersion/PreVoteDisabled and store/transport implementations are supplied by the embedding application
timers use the process clock with randomized HeartbeatTimeout/ElectionTimeout
NoLegacyTelemetry and reloadable timeouts are supplied by configuration
variants: pre-vote enabled (default when the transport implements WithPreVote) vs disabled
MonotonicLogStore vs gapped LogStore after user snapshot restore
unknowns: whether the transport heartbeat callback is expected by contract to be serialized with the main goroutine, or only to be free of the main goroutine's disk latency

activities.purpose: Form a cluster decision and advance it legally: gather support that is qualified by the current voting configuration, and only advance the commit index for entries a quorum has stored when this leader may commit them.
activities.realization_summary: A candidate becomes leader only after grantedVotes reaches quorumSize() (or pre-vote grants first reach the same quorum); a leader records each voter's acknowledged match index in commitment.matchIndexes and commitment.recalculate advances commitIndex only when the majority match index is at least commitment.startIndex, the first index created in the leader's own term. Followers advance their own commit index only from the leader's LeaderCommitIndex bounded by their own last index.

activities.purpose: Keep the election-term and leadership context valid, and acquire, transfer or lose authority only through the term/leader fields that every subsequent decision is evaluated against.
activities.realization_summary: Inbound AppendEntries/RequestVote/InstallSnapshot adopt a strictly greater term and drop to Follower; accepted AppendEntries/InstallSnapshot record the leader identity; requestVote/requestPreVote reject support while a different leader is known; checkLeaderLease steps the leader down when it cannot contact a quorum within LeaderLeaseTimeout; TimeoutNow moves authority by putting the target into Candidate with candidateFromLeadershipTransfer. NetworkTransport can additionally drive the AppendEntries term/leader update from a connection goroutine through the heartbeat callback.

activities.purpose: Recover and resynchronize a participant that cannot be caught up by log replay, and re-establish eligible participation.
activities.realization_summary: When setPreviousLog cannot find an index the leader sends the newest snapshot with sendLatestSnapshot/InstallSnapshot; the follower streams it to a SnapshotSink, restores the FSM through fsmMutateCh, then sets lastApplied/lastSnapshot/configuration and truncates logs. NewRaft restores the newest usable snapshot at start.

activities.purpose: Maintain the configuration that decides who is a participant and whose support counts.
activities.realization_summary: Configuration changes are accepted only while the latest configuration is committed and this leader has committed an entry of its own term; nextConfiguration derives the new configuration and checkConfiguration rejects an empty/duplicated participant set or a configuration without a voter; the new configuration is written as a LogConfiguration entry, applied to configurations.latest, pushed into commitment.setConfiguration and used to start/stop replication.

activities.purpose: Apply committed decisions to the client FSM in commit order and report completion to callers.
activities.realization_summary: processLogs converts committed indices into commitTuple batches (LogCommand/LogBarrier/LogConfiguration) and hands them to fsmMutateCh; the fsm goroutine applies them through FSM.Apply or BatchingFSM.ApplyBatch and responds to the logFuture, and snapshot requests report the last applied index/term.

activities.purpose: Persist and reconstruct the history that support is evaluated against (term, vote, log, configuration).
activities.realization_summary: setCurrentTerm and persistVote write StableStore before the in-memory state changes; dispatchLogs writes the leader's new entries to the LogStore before notifying replicators; NewRaft reloads the term, last log and snapshots and replays configuration entries from the log to rebuild configurations.latest/committed; snapshotting persists FSM state and compacts logs.

activities.purpose: Expose the client contract: which node may be asked to act, what completion means, and what leader identity is reported.
activities.realization_summary: Apply/ApplyLog/Barrier enqueue a logFuture and complete when the FSM path responds; VerifyLeader drives an immediate heartbeat round and completes when a quorum answers; Leader/LeaderWithID report the stored leader identity under leaderLock; CommitIndex/AppliedIndex export the internal indices.

behaviors.execution_owner: the candidate's raft main goroutine (runCandidate, then preElectSelf or electSelf)
behaviors.protocol_context: leader election with pre-vote when the transport implements WithPreVote and candidateFromLeadershipTransfer is not set

the latest configuration is not a stable non-voter configuration

responses with a term greater than the proposed term fall back to Follower

StableStore LastVoteTerm/LastVoteCand for the local vote

the real election persists a self-vote before requesting votes

the self-vote is persisted for the proposed term without comparing it with the record that may already exist for that term, and the transfer path keeps pre-vote from filtering this campaign, so a published term that has dropped below a recorded vote's term lets the campaign propose exactly that term, overwrite the record and collect a quorum while another voter's record for it is still empty

the proposed term is derived from the published current term, and that value can be lowered by an out-of-order write from another entry point, so the proposal depends on a value that is not monotonic across entry points
existing_protections: the vote-granting path refuses a second different vote in the same term by comparing the record with the request, so the rule is enforced on that path only

the response term is not inspected here: only the reads and writes listed above are performed, so a request whose term is older than the node's own is rejected by the term comparison while an equal or greater one reaches the writes

facts.meaning: The node has adopted election term T as its durable current term, and every subsequent vote grant, append-entries acceptance, pre-vote answer and leadership decision is evaluated against T. A vote is only re-granted for the same (T, candidate), and RPCs with a term below T are ignored.
facts.validity_context: Holds from the moment T is persisted until a strictly greater term is adopted. The library's design assumes the adopted value never decreases.
facts.durability: setCurrentTerm writes StableStore first and panics if that fails, then updates the in-memory atomic
facts.recovery: NewRaft reloads the term from StableStore before any goroutine starts

facts.meaning: The node's stored leader identity is (leaderAddr, leaderID), being the leader that last contacted it in the adopted term; the identity is used to reject vote and pre-vote requests while another leader is known and is reported to clients through Leader/LeaderWithID and Stats.
facts.validity_context: Cleared by every state transition, because setState clears the leader before changing state, and replaced by each accepted AppendEntries or InstallSnapshot.
facts.durability: in-memory only; not persisted across restarts
facts.recovery: relearned from the next accepted AppendEntries or InstallSnapshot

facts.meaning: The node's durable log agrees with the leader's log through index I at term T, with any conflicting local suffix already removed.
facts.validity_context: Established only after StoreLogs/DeleteRange completed on the main goroutine, or after a snapshot install placed the state at I; superseded when a later term rewrites the suffix.
facts.recovery: rebuilt by InstallSnapshot or by the NewRaft log scan

facts.meaning: The leader's commitment table records that voter V stores the leader's log through index I, which is the support the leader may count toward a commit decision.
facts.validity_context: Usable for commitment only while V is a Voter in configurations.latest; a new configuration rebuilds the table from the old values.
facts.durability: in-memory and per leader term; a new commitment is created on each leadership acquisition
facts.recovery: not recovered; re-derived from the next successful AppendEntries or InstallSnapshot responses

facts.meaning: The node has durably recorded the vote (T, C) for election term T; a duplicate request for the same (T, C) is re-granted from this record, and a request for a different candidate in T is refused.
facts.validity_context: Holds for the adopted term T; adopting a greater term makes the record unusable for new grants because the duplicate check only matches the request term.
facts.durability: persisted through StableStore before the vote is granted; a persistence error leaves the vote ungranted
facts.recovery: read back on each RequestVote; not rebuilt from any other state

facts.meaning: The node's latest configuration is the set of servers and suffrages in effect for it, together with the log index at which that configuration was established: the leader writes it when it appends a configuration entry, and followers adopt it from the log or from an installed snapshot.
facts.validity_context: Holds from the moment the configuration is established until a later configuration entry replaces it; its index identifies where it was written and is the same index a snapshot records with the configuration.
representation: configurations.latest and latestIndex on the main goroutine
a copy in Raft.latestConfiguration for readers outside the main loop
facts.durability: carried in the log entry or snapshot that established it
facts.recovery: rebuilt by NewRaft from the snapshot and the log scan, and by installSnapshot from the leader's snapshot

facts.meaning: The node's commit index is I: an entry at I has been stored by a quorum of the current voting configuration and may be applied to the FSM.
facts.validity_context: On a leader, indices before commitment.startIndex cannot be advanced by match indexes alone, so at least one entry of the leader's own term must be replicated first; on a follower the value is min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex).
representation: configurations.committedIndex when the committed entry is a configuration
facts.durability: in-memory only; the FSM state may be persisted by the caller
facts.recovery: not recovered across restarts; re-committed by the next leader

surfaces.reason: The interface lets a transport run the registered callback on its own goroutine; this module implements the fast path only in NetworkTransport and InmemTransport ignores the call, so the concurrency contract of other transports is unread.
The shape test on the decoded AppendEntriesRequest decides whether the RPC bypasses the main consumer channel, which is the entry point of the selected Candidate.
removeOldLogs and compactLogsWithTrailing were read only at the call sites used by the snapshot behaviors; the effect of a non-monotonic store on history reconstruction is not mapped here.
These are separate Go modules with their own go.mod files and are outside the single module selected for execution.

Selected and answered in scope: the obligation c-reported-configuration-index fixed the index the accessor reports against the log index at which the configuration it returns was established, and a served check observed a reported index of zero while the configuration had been established at index 1 with the returned configuration still current. The entry stays mapped to the client contract behavior that reports it.

Read while tracing the recovery path: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never advances raftState.commitIndex, so a follower that installs a snapshot at index J reports CommitIndex() below AppliedIndex() until the next AppendEntries carries a commit index. The snapshot content is committed state and CommitIndex is documented as the basis for the read-index optimisation, so the exported value under-reports the commit point; retained with its sources rather than selected.

formation.explanation: Qualified support is gathered before a decision is formed. A candidate counts granted votes (or pre-vote grants) and only becomes leader when the count reaches quorumSize(); the leader then records each voter's acknowledged match index through commitment.match, and commitment.recalculate advances commitIndex only when the majority match index is at least commitment.startIndex, the first index created in the leader's own term, so entries of earlier terms are never committed on match indexes alone. Followers advance their own commit index only from the leader's LeaderCommitIndex bounded by their own last index.

context.explanation: The context that qualifies support and authority is the adopted term plus the known leader identity. Inbound AppendEntries/RequestVote/InstallSnapshot ignore older terms and adopt a strictly greater one by writing StableStore and dropping to Follower; accepted AppendEntries/InstallSnapshot then record the leader identity, which requestVote/requestPreVote use to refuse support while a different leader is known. A leader loses authority locally through checkLeaderLease when it cannot contact a quorum of voters within LeaderLeaseTimeout, and gains it at the target through TimeoutNow, which puts the target into Candidate with candidateFromLeadershipTransfer. The same term/leader update is additionally reachable from a NetworkTransport connection goroutine through the registered heartbeat callback.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the term and at the own-term replication rule. A durable vote record is only re-granted for the same (term, candidate) and is otherwise superseded once a greater term is adopted, so support gathered in term T cannot be consumed in term T+1; conversely an RPC whose term is older than the adopted term is ignored, so a deposed leader cannot re-establish authority. On the leader side, a follower's match index only becomes usable support after the leader has matched a quorum at or beyond commitment.startIndex, so pending work from an earlier term constrains what the new leader may commit; and leadership transfer explicitly requires the target's nextIndex to be past the leader's lastIndex before TimeoutNow, so an up-to-date support context is a precondition for moving authority. Because both lines read and write the same current-term context, an entry point that updates that context outside the main goroutine (the transport heartbeat callback) is the point where the connection is not obviously serialized.

open_details: The pre-vote grant path was read at the level needed for the context path; its interaction with a concurrently observed leader was not traced to completion.
Verification reads (VerifyLeader/verifyFuture) and their quorum accounting were not traced to completion; they are represented only through the client contract activity.
Snapshot-driven log truncation was read at its call sites; the interaction with a MonotonicLogStore implementation is recorded as a deferred surface.
core_overview.rationale: Both core relationships and their connection are explained from actual code: formation and advancement are grounded in the vote tally, the pre-vote round, commitment.match/recalculate and the startIndex own-term rule; context and authority are grounded in the term/state update, leader identity update, the leader lease step-down and TimeoutNow. The connection is sourced: votes are only re-granted for the same term, older-term RPCs are ignored, match indexes are only usable at or after startIndex, and a transfer requires the target to be caught up. Three mechanisms that earlier versions of this map left as unknowns are now recorded where they belong: the transport heartbeat callback performs its term, state and leader writes without being serialized with the main goroutine and publishes the term through a plain atomic store; a client future for VerifyLeader or a batched Apply carries no shutdown escape once a completed Shutdown has left the buffered request channels unprocessed; and the candidate's self-vote is written for the proposed term without comparing it with the vote record, so a published term that has dropped by one makes the next election propose a term that already holds a vote and overwrite it while the transfer exemption keeps the campaign from being filtered. The third links to the first: the overwritten record is the only barrier the vote path's exemption leaves, so the only questions still open on this line are whether the resulting dual leadership can be made to persist and whether it can commit conflicting entries. The counter-parts that bound each mechanism are recorded beside them (the fast path cannot append logs or advance the commit index; the default unbuffered applyCh always completes and the leader lease and the replication path cover term discovery; the vote-granting path still refuses a second different vote in one term and a leader refuses a transfer request whose vote it already recorded), so no core gap is claimed and the overview stays usable.
